title: Support opencode 2.x tool ids in the opencode guard and its registry gate
action: The declared suite is red on this machine: every_registered_write_or_read_capable_opencode_tool_is_mapped_or_named_as_a_gap panics because the installed opencode is 2.2.5 (package @opencode/cli, ELF at $(mise which opencode) resolved), and its tool-id Set literal is now ["shell","glob","read","grep","webfetch","websearch","write","edit","subagent","execute","patch","todowrite","question","skill"] (1.18.x had bash/task/apply_patch). The binary also carries a rename map {bash:"shell",task:"subagent",apply_patch:"patch"}. CI pins opencode-ai@1.18.16, so the derivation must keep passing on 1.18.x AND pass on 2.x. Step 1: find out from the 2.2.5 binary which id a plugin's tool.execute.before hook receives in 2.x (old or new name). Step 2: if 2.x hands the new ids to plugins, make mapToolCall in .opencode/plugins/bee-guard.ts route shell like bash and patch like apply_patch (check if bee-guard.ts is generated from a template: rg for its source and run bee dev regen if so; also check the Rust write_guard accepts the tool_name the plugin forwards). Step 3: make derive_opencode_tool_registry accept either Set literal shape and re-check every additional/unmapped anchor against 2.x; a tool that is new in 2.x and file-capable is mapped or named as a gap in discovery.md on its own line. Keep the test hard-failing when no opencode binary is readable. Record what you found in step 1 in the cap report. If bee-guard.ts changes, run bee dev regen in this cell (render-skill-trees, onboard --repo-root . --apply, release-manifest --write) and commit the manifest.
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test opencode_plugin_contracts && .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check
verify_owner: main (feature close) — the worker never runs this

truths: the opencode registry gate passes against the installed opencode 2.2.5
the registry derivation still accepts the opencode 1.18.x Set literal
every write- or shell-capable opencode 2.x tool id is routed by mapToolCall or named as a gap in discovery.md

artifacts.substantive: derivation handles both shapes, no skip added

prohibitions: No new skip path or env switch that lets the gate pass without a readable binary
No code comments (no_code_comments): explain in discovery.md or the cap report
open_choices: How the derivation detects which literal shape is present

trace.outcome: Registry gate derives from both opencode 1.18.x and 2.x Set literals; 2.x ids named as gaps; 2.x does not load the 1.x bee-guard.ts plugin
deviations: found a better route: step 1 showed 2.x hands new ids (shell/patch/subagent) to execute.before hooks, but its loader accepts only default {id, effect|setup}; bee-guard.ts default-exports a 1.x hook function, so it never loads on 2.x. A case shell/patch alias in mapToolCall would be false coverage, so bee-guard.ts is untouched (decision 31ba5052 allows the named-gap path) and no regen/manifest change was needed
2.x also renames write/edit/read args filePath->path and moves hook args to input; porting the belt to the 2.x {id, setup} API is proposed as follow-up work

2.x registry adds additional anchors artifact_create, artifact_update, schedule_create (experimental flag), named as gaps; webfetch/websearch/todowrite/skill named as exclusions since 2.x tools are never classified safe by a filePath scan
trace.verification_evidence: 10 passed against installed @opencode/cli 2.2.5 (cargo from ~/.cargo/bin on the default PATH); the 1.18.x shape is pinned by a new synthetic-text unit test because no 1.18 binary is on this machine; release-manifest --check matched 600 files; only the test file and discovery.md changed
trace.verify_command: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test opencode_plugin_contracts && .bee/bin/bee dev release-manifest --check

mistakes.wrong: ran cargo test with a hand-built PATH that put mise shims first, so command -v resolved the mise ELF and the gate reported no Set literal
mistakes.better: run the proof with the default PATH
